key_insight: Warm-start quality for simplex is not determined just by fewer pivots: the same-quality start can have very different linear-algebra cost, so the paper learns starts using measured solver cost, not iteration count alone.
engineering_relevance: For LP solvers in practice, optimizing the warm start can cut wall-clock time substantially, making learned initialization more useful for real workloads than pivot reduction alone.
method: Predict a candidate optimal basis with a supervised model.
Train a small policy on measured instruction counts to choose how many predicted columns to use, plus algorithm and pricing rule.
Optionally skip warm-starting when it is not cost-effective.
evidence_signal: Across 25 LP classes, the method cuts dual-simplex iterations by about two-thirds but only about one-third of solve time; on unseen LPs it roughly halves solve time versus the default start.
watch_item: A warm start that looks close in basis overlap may still be expensive, so deploying this approach requires cost-aware evaluation and hardware-sensitive measurement.
paper_title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
